paper.title: Neural Contextual Bandits with UCB-based Exploration

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic K-armed contextual bandit with unknown bounded reward function
unmapped: Reward r = h(x) + noise with h an arbitrary unknown function in [0,1]; analysis via the neural tangent kernel (NTK) Gram matrix H on all T*K contexts, requiring S >= sqrt(2 h^T H^{-1} h) (an NTK-RKHS-type norm bound); kernel_rkhs is an approximation of this structure
Contexts: K feature vectors per round, generation process unspecified; regret against per-round best action
Assumption 2: NTK matrix H >= lambda_0 I, ||x||_2 = 1 and [x]_j = [x]_{j+d/2}
settings.definition_quote: We consider the stochastic $K$-armed contextual bandit problem, where the total number of rounds $T$ is known. At round $t \in [T]$, the agent observes the context consisting of $K$ feature vectors ... $r_{t,a_t} = h(\xb_{t,a_t}) + \xi_t$, where $h$ is an unknown function satisfying $0 \leq h(\xb) \leq 1$ for any $\xb$, and $\xi_t$ is $\nu$-sub-Gaussian noise conditioned on $\xb_{1,a_1},\dots,\xb_{t-1,a_{t-1}}$

symbols.d_tilde: effective dimension of the NTK matrix, log det(I + H/lambda)/log(1+TK/lambda)
symbols.J: number of gradient descent steps in TrainNN

conditions: Assumption 2: NTK matrix H >= lambda_0 I on all T*K contexts; ||x||_2 = 1 and [x]_j = [x]_{j+d/2}
h(x) in [0,1]; noise nu-sub-Gaussian conditionally on the past

source.label: thm:newalgorithm
source.quote: There exist constant $C_1, C_2>0$, such that for any $\delta \in(0,1)$, if $m \geq \text{poly}(T, L, K, \lambda^{-1}, \lambda_0^{-1}, S^{-1}, \log(1/\delta))$, $\eta = C_1( mTL + m \lambda)^{-1}$, $\lambda \geq \max\{1, S^{-2}\}$, and $S \geq \sqrt{2\hb^\top\Hb^{-1}\hb}$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of Algorithm 1 satisfies R_T \leq 3\sqrt{T}\sqrt{\tilde d \log (1+TK/\lambda) + 2}[...] + 1.

results.notes: nu (sub-Gaussian parameter) mapped to sigma. Statement contains a typo '+ +'. Remark 8: with J ~ O~(TL/lambda), constants nu, lambda, S = sqrt(2h^T H^{-1} h), bound becomes O~(sqrt(d_tilde T) sqrt(max{d_tilde, h^T H^{-1} h})), i.e. O~(d_tilde sqrt(T)). R_T is defined as an expectation but the theorem bounds it with probability 1-delta (effectively the sum of h-gaps).

symbols.d_tilde: effective dimension of the NTK matrix

conditions: Same conditions as Theorem 5: Assumption 2, S >= sqrt(2 h^T H^{-1} h), h in [0,1]
tuning: m >= poly(T, L, K, 1/lambda, 1/lambda_0, 1/S, log T)

source.label: coro:expectation
source.quote: Under the same conditions in Theorem \ref{thm:newalgorithm}, there exists a positive constant $C$ such that \EE [R_T] \leq 2+3\sqrt{T}\sqrt{\tilde d \log (1+TK/\lambda) + 2}\cdot\bigg[\nu\sqrt{\tilde d \log (1+TK/\lambda) + 2+2\log T} + 2\sqrt{\lambda}S + (\lambda + CTL)(1- \lambda/(TL))^{J/2} \sqrt{T/\lambda}\bigg].

results.notes: Obtained from Theorem 5 with delta = 1/T. Regret defined via expected rewards, hence pseudo_regret.
